item.title: How Much Change Can an Organisation Actually Absorb?
item.description:
There is a lot of excitement around AI-enabled modernisation, and with good reason. Analysis can be accelerated, code can be generated or transformed faster, testing can be improved, and large estates that once looked prohibitively expensive to tackle can begin to look much more manageable. But that creates a new problem: if the technology can move faster, how much change can the organisation actually absorb?

That question is rarely asked clearly enough at the beginning of a modernisation programme. We tend to model engineering capacity, delivery waves, migration throughput, environments and technical dependencies in some detail, but we do not always model with the same discipline the capacity of the organisation itself to consume the change being produced. That matters because transformation is not complete when the new capability exists. It is complete when the organisation has actually moved.

item.title: Borrowing Horizons
item.description:
My seven-year-old daughter spends quite a lot of time thinking about the future, usually in the form of questions for me.

“When can I ride a motorbike?” “When can I use that power tool?” “When can I jump off that?”

Sometimes she wants a date. Is it when she’s eight? Ten? A teenager? Sometimes tomorrow seems perfectly reasonable.

What I find fascinating is the ambition behind the questions. She can imagine herself doing almost anything; what she doesn’t yet have is a particularly sophisticated understanding of the risks, dependencies or capabilities involved in getting there. Her horizon is enormous because experience hasn’t yet taught her all the reasons something might be difficult.

item.title: I love it when a plan comes together
item.description: So I thought these posts would happen more regularly; it’s just been intense getting to know so many people. Bringing together three teams distributed across our campuses has been a great deal of fun. Each is unique, with its distinct strengths and culture. Today I shared our strategy for IT across the group. While I get nervous speaking in front of people, I love these moments. It’s the big reveal of the analysis and work that has been amassed over the last 6 months. While I’m not going to share the whole presentation, I will run through the top-level framework and a couple of the guiding principles.

item.title: An Entertaining Start
item.description: So at the beginning of the month I began a new adventure as an employee for the first time in 7 years, starting as the new Group Director for IT with Eastern Colleges Group. I really am excited about this role, there is so much to get to grips with, so many areas in which IT directly contributes to the eduction delivered by the colleges. I’ll be posting sporadically (if I ever get this blog published) with how the role is going and the challeges that we face in ensuring that the systems keep working.
